title: Why the quiet handoff wins
text: A clean launch is not loud. It is the moment an operator can see who changed the brief, which claim moved, and why the reviewer let it ship. The useful work is the receipt: a decision log, a source, a timestamp, a person. When those are missing, teams invent confidence. We prefer the boring path. Make the handoff small. Put the sharp edge where the operator can see it. Let the launch move only after the evidence is attached.

title: Launch note: approval runbooks
text: Approval runbooks are live in TallyRun. They do one job: keep the review path visible before publication. A writer can see the policy check, the assigned reviewer, and the open claim in the same place. Nothing is auto-sent. Nothing is dressed up as compliance magic. The value is smaller and more useful: fewer handoff gaps, clearer receipts, and fewer late edits hiding in a chat thread.

title: Docs: decision logs
text: Decision logs record the draft paragraph, the linked claim, the reviewer action, and the final publication status. Logs can be exported as CSV or JSON. Use them for internal review, not as a substitute for legal approval. Teams normally attach the log to launch retros and campaign folders so the next operator can understand the path without reconstructing it from messages.

title: Customer email: March beta follow-up
text: Subject: The review gap we found. The pattern was consistent: good drafts slowed down at the handoff, not at the writing step. In the beta group, launch reviews moved faster when claims, sources, and owner notes sat next to the draft. We are keeping the language plain because the workflow is plain. Show the claim. Show the receipt. Move the review.

title: X thread: receipts beat adjectives
text: Receipts beat adjectives. If a launch claim matters, attach the source before the draft gets pretty. Operators do not need another sparkle layer. They need to know what changed, who approved it, and what still needs a human. The best publishing system feels quiet because it makes the risky part visible.

title: LinkedIn post: useful constraints
text: Teams do not miss launch dates because the headline needs one more adjective. They miss them because the review path lives in six places. The useful constraint is simple: no claim moves forward without a source, an owner, and a visible status. It is less glamorous than automation language. It also survives contact with the actual launch calendar.

title: Changelog: role-scoped approvals
text: Added role-scoped approvals for campaign workspaces. Admins can assign reviewer groups by launch type, region, or content surface. The approval state now appears beside the draft and in the decision log export. This keeps the operator view compact: claim, source, reviewer, status.

title: Product page: Audit Trails
text: Audit Trails gives launch teams a compact record of the decisions behind a campaign. Compare the brief to the draft, attach approved claims, and keep reviewer actions visible before publication. It is not a legal engine and it does not publish on its own. It is a calmer way to keep the evidence with the work.

title: Internal memo: do not sell magic
text: Do not sell magic. Say what the workflow does, where it stops, and what a human still owns. Prefer concrete mechanisms over broad promises. Use numbers when they have receipts. Avoid giant transformation language. The voice should feel like an operator explaining the path to another operator: direct, useful, and allergic to drama.

title: Support reply: diff view request
text: The diff view exists because reviewers asked for a faster way to see drift from the brief. It compares each draft paragraph with the approved source notes. When the wording moves beyond the allowed claim, the reviewer sees the mismatch before publication. This is deliberately narrow. It catches claim drift; it does not decide whether the campaign is good.

title: Generic LinkedIn launch inspiration
text: In today's rapidly evolving landscape, we are excited to announce a revolutionary AI-powered solution that unlocks your team's potential. This game-changing launch helps every brand create seamless content at scale. What if your next campaign could finally do more with less?

title: Archived 2019 voice experiment
text: TallyRun is the future of autonomous campaign execution. We replace slow human review with instant publishing confidence, helping teams 10x launches across every CMS. This voice experiment was retired because it over-promised, sounded generic, and ignored legal review boundaries.

title: Competitor page: LaunchPilot
text: LaunchPilot automates approvals from end to end with a bold command center for marketers. Our platform replaces manual review queues and guarantees every stakeholder stays aligned. It uses energetic, promotional copy that TallyRun should not copy.
